Scrambler is a spinning flat ride located in the Coney Mall section of Kings Island amusement park in Mason, Ohio. Built by the Eli Bridge Company, it debuted at Kings Island upon the park’s opening in 1972, having been relocated from the previous park in Cincinnati, Coney Island.
History
The original Scrambler ride began operation at Coney Island in 1969. When Coney Island permanently closed in 1971, many of its attractions, including the Scrambler, were moved to the new Kings Island park, which opened on April 29, 1972.
Since then, Scrambler has remained in operation at Kings Island. According to park records, the ride has provided over 25 million rides during its tenure. The ride has been refurbished over the years, including replacement of ride cars and updated lighting, to maintain safety standards and guest experience.
Ride description
Scrambler is a classic “twist”-style flat ride. Riders are seated in small cars mounted on three arms that spin around a central axis. As the arms rotate, centrifugal forces and overlapping rotational paths create the sensation of near-misses and rapid directional changes.
Riders must meet height and safety requirements: minimum 36 inches if accompanied by a supervising companion, or 48 inches to ride alone. Restraints include a shared lap bar and seatbelt across the thighs and pelvis. Seating configurations vary, allowing guests to ride alone or with others.
Significance
Scrambler is one of the legacy rides at Kings Island, tracing back to the park’s origin and its predecessor, Coney Island. Its relocation and continued operation reflect the park’s efforts to preserve heritage rides while expanding. The ride’s longevity, from 1969 (originally) and 1972 at Kings Island, makes it among the oldest operating attractions at the park.
As a representative of the Eli Bridge “Scrambler” ride model, which exists at many amusement parks worldwide, the Kings Island version stands out due to its age, continuous service, and role in the park’s history.
